verdict.rationale: The managed-agent skill explicitly translates natural-language requests into structured Buzz CLI actions (e.g., 'When someone naturally asks to create an agent... run: buzz agents draft-create...'), and the ACP harness lets agents interpret @mention conversation and reply via the CLI, showing genuine NL-to-command operation. However this is demonstrated mainly for agent-creation and messaging flows rather than the full breadth of product operations, and most CLI examples (buzz-docs-5/6/7/8) are structured, not NL. Missing for 10: evidence of NL commands covering the full CLI surface (repos, workflows, channels beyond agent creation), and independent/hands-on confirmation that NL parsing works reliably in practice.
